active_themes.label: Talks Over Tankers
active_themes.summary: Trump said today he's 'hopefully towards end' of the Iran war — the first public signal in a while that the conflict driving oil-linked inflation pressure might be nearing resolution. Nothing in tanker traffic or Brent pricing confirms this yet; it's a rhetorical opening, not a fact on the ground. Whether it translates into actual Hormuz traffic or lower oil is the test.

active_themes.label: AI Trade Loses Its Shield
active_themes.summary: After more than four sessions of the Nasdaq underperforming the Dow, today reversed sharply — Nasdaq flat, Dow down over a point — the first break in that pattern since it emerged. It's one session, and the cause could be the hike removing uncertainty rather than a genuine change in tech's footing. The next session or two will tell you whether this is real relief or noise.

active_themes.label: The Fix Unwound
active_themes.summary: No new yield print came through today, so the 19-year-high level from day 123 stands as the last known data point. The Fed's hike changes the calculus going forward — a hike normally pushes short-term rates up while long-term yields can go either way depending on whether the market believes inflation gets tamed or gets worse. The next yield close is now the most important number in this entire brief.

active_themes.label: Fed Voices Split
active_themes.summary: The anticipated hike arrived today, unanimous, with Kevin Warsh declaring 'inflation is too high and has been for too long' and the Fed signaling a second hike is likely this year. Trump responded by demanding rates fall to '1% or less' and lashing out publicly — the independence tension this theme has tracked for 154 days is no longer theoretical, it played out in real time today. What's open now: whether the Fed actually delivers that second hike into a supply-driven inflation problem, and whether political pressure escalates beyond rhetoric.

open_watchlist.condition: Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz shows any rebound from today's single-digit levels.
open_watchlist.meaning: If it stays near zero, this is a confirmed physical supply shock, not a fear premium, and oil's floor above $100 becomes much harder to dislodge.

open_watchlist.condition: Kevin Warsh or another Fed official publicly addresses oil-driven inflation the way the ECB just did.
open_watchlist.meaning: Fed language matching the ECB's would signal the US is leaning toward a hold or hike over a cut, repricing rate-cut bets across markets.

open_watchlist.condition: Brent crude either falls back below $100 or extends its climb toward $110 over the next several sessions.
open_watchlist.meaning: A pullback would ease the inflation story industry-wide; a push higher would spread the ECB's hawkish logic to more central banks.

open_watchlist.condition: Brent crude either breaks above $110 or falls back under $100 over the next several sessions.
open_watchlist.meaning: Above $110 means the inflation and Fed-hike story gets worse from here; under $100 means today's calm was justified.

open_watchlist.condition: The 10-year Treasury yield closes above 5.25% or drops back under 5% in the sessions following the Fed decision.
open_watchlist.meaning: Tells us whether 5% was a ceiling that holds or a floor the market keeps pushing through.

open_watchlist.condition: The Dow-Nasdaq performance gap widens or closes over the next several sessions, especially on a day when yields ease.
open_watchlist.meaning: Shows whether the AI-linked tech decoupling is now a durable rotation away from tech or just tracking the broader yield stress.

open_watchlist.condition: The Nasdaq outperforms the Dow again in the next session, following today's reversal of the multi-day pattern.
open_watchlist.meaning: Would confirm tech is finding genuine relief now that the rate path is known, not just a one-day quirk.

open_watchlist.condition: The 10-year Treasury yield's next close — whether it holds above 5% or breaks back under it after the hike.
open_watchlist.meaning: Tells you whether bond investors believe the Fed just tamed inflation or just made the growth outlook worse.

open_watchlist.condition: Brent crude either breaks above $110 or falls back under $100 in the sessions following today's hike.
open_watchlist.meaning: This is the number that decides whether the Fed's next move is a pause or a second hike into a supply shock.

open_watchlist.condition: Any actual shift in Hormuz tanker traffic following Trump's comment that the Iran war is 'towards an end.'
open_watchlist.meaning: Would be the first real evidence that de-escalation talk is translating into lower physical oil-supply risk, not just rhetoric.
